author: YUAN X

theorems.statement: For every nonzero pair (a,b), C[a:b]=((a^2-b^2)+J*2ab)/(a^2+b^2) has character norm one because (a^2-b^2)^2+(2ab)^2=(a^2+b^2)^2.
theorems.boundary: The J-character plane is a derived rotation representation and is not identified with the native Enterprise metric plane.

theorems.statement: Under [a:b] star [c:d]=[ac-bd:ad+bc], norms multiply and C(u star v)=C(u)C(v). Scaling or simultaneous sign reversal of a pair does not change its character.
Every rational point (x,y) with x^2+y^2=1 is C[1+x:y] when x is not -1, while (-1,0)=C[0:1]. Thus P1(Q) parametrizes the rational unit-character conic.
C[1:0]=1, C[1:1]=J, C[0:1]=-1, and [1:1] star [1:1]=[0:1], so J^2=-1. Reflection exchanges [1:1] and [1:-1], hence the sign of the quarter-turn coordinate requires chirality.
For projective parameter t, C(t)=((1-t^2)+J*2t)/(1+t^2)=(1+Jt)/(1-Jt), with infinity mapped to -1, and C(s)C(t)=C((s+t)/(1-st)) in projective arithmetic.
theorems.boundary: No inverse tangent or classical angle is needed for this law.

theorems.statement: For R=Q*sqrt(D) and tau=R-P, tau=1/(R+P) and C(tau)=P/R+J/R. Thus the negative-Pell residual is exactly the Cayley half-angle coordinate of the normalized near-axis segment (P,1).
sqrt(2)-1, 13sqrt(29)-70, and 13sqrt(58)-99 are the Cayley defects of the negative-Pell segments (1,1), (70,1), and (99,1), and 99sqrt(2)-70-13sqrt(29)=(sqrt(2)-1)^6(13sqrt(29)-70)(13sqrt(58)-99).
theorems.boundary: The exponent six is not derived here from the six Cell gates.

theorems.statement: [5:1]^4 star [239:-1]=[1:1]; before projective reduction, (5+J)^4(239-J)=114244(1+J). Classical angle decoding yields Machin's identity but is not needed for the integer certificate.

On a transitive homogeneous Cell carrier, every translation-invariant direction readout from one Cell is constant. The common-translation quotient of ordered neighboring Cell pairs is instead exactly the six oriented neighbor-direction classes; endpoint swap and a chosen cyclic rotation descend to half-turn and successor operations.
theorems.boundary: This closes only the restricted primitive ordered-segment subsystem, not every native Cell trajectory.

theorems.statement: For Q_n(theta)=(1+J theta/(2n))/(1-J theta/(2n)), every finite Q_n(theta)^n has exact unit norm and the standard limit is exp(J theta).
theorems.interpretation: The base e records the continuous completion of repeated multiplicative forward composition; it is not a spatial direction or an additional geometric primitive.

derivation or refutation of the exponent six in the N=58 defect product from six Cell gates
